newsitem.title: FRANCE: Zaire's Mobutu had radiation therapy, son says.
newsitem.headline: Zaire's Mobutu had radiation therapy, son says.

text.p: President Mobutu Sese Seko's son says the embattled Zairean ruler was given radiation therapy after prostate cancer surgery last August, a treatment medical experts say means his cancer has almost certainly spread.

Independent cancer specialists not involved in treating him say Mobutu, struggling to keep Zaire together in the face of a rebel uprising, should live for at least another two to three years with good medical care -- and could survive far longer.

Mobutu's son and spokesman Mobutu Nzanga told Reuters his father, who has ruled Zaire with an iron hand for 31 years, had received radiation therapy "a few months ago". He would not say whether it was continuing.

"These are treatment details, and I cannot go any further," the younger Mobutu said in a telephone interview on Monday. "He is in very good health, and he is not the first head of state to have prostate surgery. It is very far from critical."
One prostate specialist, speaking on condition of anonymity, said: "If he had radiation therapy, the cancer has spread... either locally or perhaps to the bone."
Other doctors agreed, based on Mobutu's long convalescence, haggard appearance and obvious weakness in his rare public appearances in recent months.

A serious spreading of the cancer could require him to take powerful painkillers that could slow his pace and affect his judgment during delicate manoeuvring on Zaire's future, medical experts and Western diplomats said.
"He has an awful lot to do. If he is in pain, one wonders how much attention he can be paying to things," said one Western diplomat who monitors developments in Zaire.
Mobutu Nzanga denied the Zairean leader was in pain. "Not at all, he's in very good shape," he said.

The radiation treatment apparently took place in Switzerland in September and October, while Mobutu remained in seclusion following his August 22 prostate operation. A typical course of therapy takes about eight weeks.
Mobutu left Lausanne on November 4 for his palatial Riviera villa in the French resort of Roquebrune-Cap Martin.
Since going home to Zaire in mid-December, Mobutu has returned to southern France regularly for visits to the Princess Grace Hospital in Monaco, aides confirmed.
They said the president had visited the Monaco hospital on November 25, January 10, January 18 and February 22.
Mobutu Nzanga said all of the visits were for routine medical checks and tests. He said his father's doctors did not intend to issue a statement or be interviewed on his health.
"He has a very important role to play for Zaire. He was operated on in August, and you saw the consequences...Opponents took the opportunity to attack Zaire," Mobutu Nzanga said.
Mobutu's ragged army is floundering against Ugandan-backed rebels of the Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire, who have captured a swathe of eastern Zaire.

Rebel leader Laurent Kabila flew to South Africa on Tuesday for talks with President Nelson Mandela's government on the war but was said by aides to have no plans to meet representatives of the Zairean government. Mobutu Nzanga said his father opposed any negotiation with the rebels.
